keyFindings.description: `lint`, a check the base branch requires, is red at the code head e4f7f42e55a4 (Tests run 40176152122, job 121117155580). The one error is a Biome formatter error on this file: removing the `lost_detail` parameter shortened the template literal, and the `const out =` assignment must now be joined onto one line. Reproduced in the workspace: `bunx biome check scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts` → `Formatter would have printed the following content … Found 1 error`. The other two Biome diagnostics in that job (`useLiteralKeys` in packages/pi-shared/src/handoff-commit.ts, `noTemplateCurlyInString` in packages/claude-envoy/tests/dist-fresh.test.ts) are the warning and info the run also reports and are not what fails it. `bunx biome check --write` on the one file closes it.

The cutover's ordering does not hold against the daemon's own boot. This change raises DaemonAPIVersion to 36 (internal/api/version.go:320), and boot posts StalePlugin to every restored live claim whose recorded contract is not the daemon's (internal/daemon/daemon.go:1083 `refreshStalePlugins(s.claims, "boot")`, :1090-1116); refreshPlugin then calls replaceProcess "the process on another plugin contract is replaced mid-turn" (internal/supervise/plugin.go:41-54, internal/supervise/repoint.go:51). That relaunch meets supersededDisk for every issue Sandbox of the previous release (relaunch.go:526-537) and runs replaceSupersededSandbox, which deletes the Sandbox and, with it, the volume holding the issue's whole workspace. So the first boot of this release deletes every running issue's disk by itself, mid-turn, before the operator can reach step 2's "Let a role mid-turn finish, or ask it through Dispatch to push". Step 3 discloses the loss as happening "whenever that launch comes"; for a live claim that launch is the boot. The push and stop of every running issue must be placed before the earlier daemon is scaled to 0, which is the last moment an agent can be asked to push, or the migrating relaunch must be held. This is read from the code, not reproduced on a cluster.

The round-1 fix is right on the path it covers and leaves a window it does not. replaceSupersededSandbox deletes the old Sandbox, waits for the API to lose it, then creates the annotated replacement; between those two the Sandbox does not exist. The observer runs on its own ticker and takes no launch turn (watch.go:112-132), so a sibling role evaluated in that window reads `v.sandbox == nil` → Gone (observe.go:183-187), `names(nil, loc)` false, and the confirming readSandbox also returns nil (observe.go:91-107), so displaced() cannot fire and the supervisor charges a death and interrupts the turn (supervise/machine.go:1111-1115). The verdict is final and the claim is then forgotten (watch.go:129-131), so the replacement's annotation cannot repair it. A failed Create or a daemon restart in that window makes the loss permanent. The delete is foreground-propagated and waits out the claim and six Secrets, so the window is seconds rather than instants. The new regression test probes only after the replacement exists (relaunch_test.go:333-375). Remedy: have the runtime remember the displaced pod uid for the claim across the Sandbox's absence and let displaced() consult it when the Sandbox is gone. A race read from the code; not reproduced.

The corrected parked checkpoints wait for the Sandbox and pod to be gone and then assert the disk's absence once (`assert_no_pod_disk` at :3652, :3697, :3736). An issue's disk is the pod's own generic ephemeral claim, so Kubernetes reaps it after the pod object goes, not with it — the round-1 tester measured about a second on a real cluster. child1_released one block above (:3618-3623) already has the right shape: the disk is inside the bounded wait. The parked predicates should read the disk the same way, or the live proof fails on a correct stop whose claim is still being collected.

The proof's own contract now contradicts the script this round corrected. `child-release` still says of the parked child "its Sandbox is Suspended, its pod gone, and its disk gone with that pod — the Sandbox alone stays until the tree closes"; `idle-resident` says "child 2, parked in backlog, has its one Sandbox Suspended with no pod and so no disk"; `node-release` says "the root's, child 2's and child 3's Sandboxes are Suspended". The script now requires no Sandbox at all for a parked issue (child2_parked at :3647-3651, tree1_parked at :6184-6192). A maintainer reading the README to learn what the proof asserts is given the behaviour this change abolished.

Deleting the file-session mode emptied the controller's init container, and the container stayed. `workspaceController` (cmd/legion/workspace_init.go:95-108) now only checks that --root is absolute — it is the compiled-in constant TreeRoot, passed by this very manifest — and refuses a provisioning-token variable the controller's pod never sets. Every controller pod still runs a whole init container with an image, resources, a volume mount and a CLI subcommand to do that. Return no init containers for controllerPod and delete the subcommand, its tests and the golden entries; a construction invariant worth keeping belongs at the manifest boundary.

Two comments this round wrote still attribute the controller's volume to its session: manifest_test.go:1780-1781 ("a relaunch finds the session its last pod left on it") and layout_test.go:119-120 ("the controller's owns the one `issue` template its session is resumed from"). Under this change every session is a row in the session database; the controller's volume survives because its working root does, which is what those comments should say.

Census accuracy, not a gap. I re-ran all nine of the census's search commands at the code head. Eight match exactly (session_store 104, SessionDSN* 93, IssueSuspend{ 9, WorkspaceLost|InitFailed 1, WorkspaceRecoveredFrom 0, LEGION_EXPECT_ISSUE_VOLUME 9, mark-lost 5, mountsProviders 0). `SuspendIssue` reads 24 at the head against the body's 25 — the census was run at 55624814a287 and the forward merge moved the tree since. Every one of the 24 falls in a class the body lists: the interface, its one implementation, its one caller, tests, comments and e2e prose, and the one deliberate docs/solutions hit. No hit is unlisted and none lacks a disposition.
